            grace_period (float): When any processes fail, wait this long (in seconds)

                still don't exit, wait another grace period before killing them.

_pipeline_afab`. I checked it against a single-process reference model with `world_size` 1 and 2 on gloo/CPU. Parameter gradients matched the reference on every layer a rank owns. I didn't run your hook-based activation test, since it isn't in the directory.

- **Partitioning:** layers are split evenly across ranks, with any remainder going to the earlier ranks. Rank 0 also runs the embedding. The last rank also runs the final norm, `lm_head` and the loss. In my 5-layer test rank 0 ran layers 0–2 and rank 1 ran layers 3–4.
- **Forward pass:** all microbatches run first. Each stage sends its output hidden states to the next rank with `P2POp` (via `batch_isend_irecv`). Received activations get `requires_grad` so gradients can flow back through them.
- **Backward pass:** it runs over the microbatches in order 0..n-1, not reversed. The last rank calls `backward()` on its loss, which is `cross_entropy / num_microbatches`. Every other rank receives the gradient from the next rank, backpropagates it, and sends its input gradient to the previous rank.
- **Return value:** the last rank returns the summed scaled loss as a float. Other ranks return `None`.
- **No hooks, and the model is not edited:** the code calls the existing `model.model.layers[...]` modules directly, so the test's own hooks will still fire on them. It builds the causal mask and rotary embeddings the same way `LlamaModel.forward` does.
